full_judgment: 13. As it is stated above, learned advocate for the petitioner submits that mandatory pre-deposit of 10% of the demanded amount being a huge sum, petitioner being a Government corporation cannot arrange the amount from any source until and unless necessary budget allocated for this particular purpose. Though learned advocate for the petitioner raised other points on merit of the case but our apex court in the case of TaeHung packaging (BD) limited vs Bangladesh, reported in 18 BLC (AD) 144, held: "When the question of maintainability of a writ petition raised by the contesting respondents, it is the first and foremost duty of the learned Judges to decide the said question first. If the writ petitions are not found maintainable, then it will be sheer wastage of court's valuable time to consider and discuss the merit of the case".
